differences.title: 1. PRIMARY USE CASE
differences.leftDesc: Debezium is purpose-built for capturing row-level database changes (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) via transaction logs, emitting events directly from transaction boundaries.
differences.rightDesc: Kafka Connect is a framework for scalable streaming data pipelines, handling both source (ingest) and sink (eject) connectors for diverse systems, not CDC-specific.

differences.title: 2. CONNECTOR TYPE
differences.leftDesc: Debezium uses database transaction logs (e.g., PostgreSQL WAL, MongoDB oplog) to capture changes, ensuring low latency and durability.
differences.rightDesc: Kafka Connect supports plugins for any source/sink system (e.g., JDBC, S3, Elasticsearch), enabling bidirectional data flow beyond just CDC.

differences.title: 3. SETUP COMPLEXITY
differences.leftDesc: Debezium requires minimal setup: point to a database’s log, define replication slot; ideal for teams that need CDC quickly without boilerplate.
differences.rightDesc: Kafka Connect demands connector config (JSON/REST), parameter tuning for performance, throughput, and schema evolution, adding operational overhead.

differences.title: 4. EVENT STRUCTURE
differences.leftDesc: Debezium emits structured change events (before/after state, operation type) in a consistent Avro/JSON schema, simplifying downstream processing.
differences.rightDesc: Kafka Connect streams raw data from sources to sinks, with schema inferred by the connector, leading to inconsistent event formats across systems.

differences.title: 5. PERFORMANCE IMPACT
differences.leftDesc: Debezium leverages native database replication, adding minimal overhead by tapping into low-level event streams rather than polling.
differences.rightDesc: Kafka Connect connectors (e.g., JDBC) often poll for changes, introducing latency and load, especially with large tables or frequent queries.

differences.title: 6. ERROR HANDLING
differences.leftDesc: Debezium tracks offsets in the database log, allowing resuming from last committed position even after restarts, ensuring no event loss.
differences.rightDesc: Kafka Connect relies on connector-specific error handling; failures may require manual intervention, schema drift, or data loss if not configured properly.

differences.title: 7. INTEGRATION ECOSYSTEM
differences.leftDesc: Debezium is tightly integrated with Kafka; events are published to topics, enabling seamless stream processing with Kafka Streams or ksqlDB.
differences.rightDesc: Kafka Connect connects Kafka to any system (S3, BigQuery, etc.), but lacks native support for stream processing, requiring additional tooling for transformations.
